options.editor.syncNote: Request learning needs one source request to capture credentials first. If the values are not available from storage or cookies, the first run uses learning mode and the next run applies the redirect.
options.editor.requestLearning.desc: Sniffs credentials from the first network request. Requires double-refreshing the page to apply. Best for traditional web apps.
options.editor.browserStorage.desc: Reads tokens directly from Local/Session Storage. Instant redirects without double-refreshing. Best for React/Vue SPA.
options.editor.cookie.desc: Reads credentials directly from session Cookies. Instant redirects without double-refreshing. Best for cookie-based auth.

options.help.title: Help
options.help.storageArea.title: Storage Area
options.help.storageArea.content: Select where the target website stores its authentication data. You can check this by pressing F12 (DevTools) > Application tab > Storage > Local Storage or Session Storage.
options.help.authPrefix.title: Prefix (Optional)
options.help.authPrefix.content: A prefix added to the token before it is sent in the Authorization Header. Usually set to Bearer (don't forget the trailing space if needed).
options.help.authKey.title: Authorization Key
options.help.authKey.content: The key name that stores the authorization token value in your selected Storage Area. For example, access_token or jwt_token.
options.help.cookies.title: Cookie Names
options.help.cookies.content: A comma-separated list of cookie names you want to extract and transfer automatically. Check DevTools > Application tab > Cookies. Example: _session_id, xsrf_token
options.help.headers.title: Headers Storage Key
options.help.headers.content: The key name in the Storage Area containing a JSON object of additional headers you want to synchronize.
options.help.ruleName.title: Rule Name
options.help.ruleName.content: A human-readable name to easily identify this rule in the list.
options.help.ruleGroup.title: Group
options.help.ruleGroup.content: An optional label to organize related rules together so the list looks tidy (e.g. API Staging or Auth Headers).
options.help.patternType.title: Pattern Format
options.help.patternType.content: Select Wildcard for simple matching (using * as a wildcard), or Regex for high-precision matching that supports capture groups (like $1).
options.help.sourcePattern.title: Source URL Pattern
options.help.sourcePattern.content: The URL pattern that will be intercepted by the extension. If a request matches this pattern, it will be redirected to the Target URL.
options.help.targetUrl.title: Redirect Target URL
options.help.targetUrl.content: The destination URL. You can use group variables (such as $1, $2) if Pattern Format is set to Regex.
options.help.credentialMode.title: Credential Mode
options.help.credentialMode.content: Choose Manual to write authentication headers yourself, or Sync from source to automatically extract and transfer credentials from the source application to the target URL.
options.help.manualAuthorization.title: Manual Authorization
options.help.manualAuthorization.content: Write exactly the value you want to send as the Authorization header to the Target URL (e.g., Bearer my_static_token).
options.help.manualCookies.title: Manual Cookies
options.help.manualCookies.content: Add specific cookie names and values that you want to manually inject into the request heading to the Target URL.
options.help.manualHeaders.title: Manual Headers
options.help.manualHeaders.content: Add other custom HTTP headers (besides Authorization) required by the Target URL.
options.help.credentialSource.title: Credential Source
options.help.credentialSource.content:
Determines the authentication data retrieval method.

Request learning: Sniffs credentials from live network requests.
Browser storage: Reads tokens from the target's Local/Session Storage.
Cookies: Reads credentials from Cookies.
options.help.syncTargets.title: Data to Inject
options.help.syncTargets.content: Check which elements you want to inject into the destination request (Additional Headers, Authorization, or Session Cookies).
